answer: The onyx lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the plume is where a second reviewer recomputes them. By the meadow of the epoch the only identities still standing are the ones whose work held up. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. The design leans on per-epoch sampling audit, re-queued for a second panel, no identity may audit its own recruit. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
